title: Close one road: does the map split?
hook: Close one road at a time. For how many of the seven does the map fall apart?

knows: depth-first search visits every town it can reach (maze-depth-first)
a map of towns and roads is a graph
doesNotKnow: that some single roads are critical (bridges) and others are not
how to tell which ones they are

misconception: The busiest town's roads are the weak points, and closing almost any road matters.
objective: The learner can explain that a road is a bridge exactly when it lies on no loop, so in the map made of triangle 1-2-3, road 3-4 and triangle 4-5-6 only closing 3-4 splits the network, and that depth-first search can find all bridges in one pass.

claims.text: On this map (triangle 1-2-3, road 3-4, triangle 4-5-6), closing 3-4 cuts towns 4, 5 and 6 off from 1, 2 and 3; closing any of the other six roads leaves every town reachable.
claims.source: Demo.tsx reach() flood-fills from town 1 with each road removed, the same code the stage uses; builder re-ran it in a separate node script (scratchpad algo2b0/check.mjs), 2026-10-14: only 3-4 leaves 3 of 6 towns reachable. Matches brief cs.algorithms #76. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Re-ran Demo.tsx reach() for each road: only 3-4 leaves {1,2,3}; others reach all 6.

claims.text: Towns 3 and 4 each touch three roads, yet closing any of their other roads changes nothing: those roads sit on loops, so traffic goes the other way round.
claims.source: Degree count from Demo.tsx ROADS (town 3: 2-3, 1-3, 3-4; town 4: 3-4, 4-5, 4-6); flood-fill result as in c1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Degrees from ROADS: town 3 = 3, town 4 = 3; closing 2-3, 1-3, 4-5, 4-6 keeps all 6. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G): r7: 'triangle road beside them' named a triangle the tangled v2 drawing no longer shows; reworded to 'their other roads ... sit on loops'. Same fact (2-3, 1-3, 4-5, 4-6 are each on a loop). | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own flood fill: closing each road leaves 6, 6, 6, 3, 6, 6, 6 towns reachable (only 3-4 splits). Town 3 roads 2-3, 1-3, 3-4; town 4 roads 3-4, 4-5, 4-6; each of 2-3, 1-3, 4-5, 4-6 lies on a triangle (1-2-3 or 4-5-6), so a detour exists.

claims.text: A road on a loop has a detour; a bridge is a road on no loop.
claims.source: If edge u-v lies on a cycle, the rest of the cycle is a u..v path without it, so removing it disconnects nothing. If removing u-v leaves a u..v path, that path plus u-v is a cycle. CLRS 4e ch. 20 problem 20-2 (articulation points, bridges and biconnected components). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Cycle/detour equivalence re-derived (both directions). | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 drops the trailing 'so it has none' (same content). Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Derivation: an edge uv is on a cycle iff u and v stay connected without it; on stage brute force (own node) only 3-4 disconnects (3 of 6 reachable), the other six each lie on a triangle.

claims.text: A depth-first walk finds the bridge in one pass: from town 1 (highest-numbered neighbour first) town 4 is visited #3, and the earliest visit anything from there on can loop back to is #3 (↩#3); town 3, #2, came earlier and no loop reaches it, so no other road gets around 3-4.
claims.source: Tarjan (1974), 'A note on finding the bridges of a graph', Information Processing Letters 2(6); low-link values: tree edge (u, v) is a bridge iff low[v] > disc[u]. CLRS 4e ch. 20, problem 20-2. Runs in linear time O(V + E). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Implemented low-link DFS (bridge iff low[v] > disc[u]) on this map: returns only 3-4. Tarjan (1974) IPL 2(6) and CLRS 4e problem 20-2 cited from memory, not opened; the description matches the standard algorithm. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 replaces the told algorithm sentence with the walk drawn on stage ('Walk depth-first' shows #visit and ↑#low per town; 3-4 drawn thick as the tree road with low[child] > disc[parent]). Builder's node run of DFS in Demo.tsx: disc 1:1, 3:2, 4:3, 6:4, 5:5, 2:6; low 1:1, 3:1, 2:1, 4:3, 6:3, 5:3; tree 1-3, 3-4, 4-6, 6-5, 3-2; bridges [3-4]. Rule low[v] > disc[u] per Tarjan 1974 (pass 21 implemented it independently). Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own DFS copy (neighbours high first): disc 1:1, 3:2, 4:3, 6:4, 5:5, 2:6; low[4] = 3 > disc[3] = 2, so 3-4 is the only bridge (matches brute force). Reveal template gives 'town 4 was visited #3 ... ↑#3. Town 3 is #2'. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G): r7: 'climbs back higher than #3' read backwards (higher meant smaller). Now 'earliest visit it can loop back to', mark changed from ↑ to ↩. Same low-link values (disc 4 = 3, low 4 = 3, disc 3 = 2). The values also sit in a stage row 'Walk: town 4 #3 ↩#3, town 3 #2. Bridge: 3–4.' | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own DFS copy (neighbours high first): disc 1:1, 3:2, 4:3, 6:4, 5:5, 2:6; low 1:1, 3:1, 2:1, 4:3, 6:3, 5:3; only tree road with low[child] > disc[parent] is 3-4 (3 > 2), matching brute force. low[4] = 3 is the smallest visit number reachable from 4's subtree by one non-tree road (4-5 back to #3), so "earliest visit ... can loop back to is #3" is the low-link value read correctly. Reveal and Walk row strings regenerated: "town 4 #3 ↩#3, town 3 #2. Bridge: 3–4."

claims.text: Coloured towns can still be reached from town 1; red towns are cut off.
claims.source: Stage convention: Demo.tsx colours towns in reach(closed) with var(--domain), others var(--bad). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Demo.tsx fills reach(closed) towns var(--domain), others var(--bad).

claims.text: Stage: after 'Walk depth-first' each town shows its visit number and the earliest visit number it can loop back to (#visit ↩#earliest), with the legend 'Depth-first from 1. #visit order; ↩ earliest # it loops back to. Dotted: road back.'; dotted roads are the two roads the walk did not travel down (1-2 and 4-5), and 3-4 is marked as the bridge.
claims.source: Demo.tsx v2 DFS (see c4): non-tree roads are 1-2 and 4-5 (dotted); badges render DFS.disc and DFS.low; bridge 3-4 drawn in var(--domain), width 6. Builder, 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own DFS: tree roads 1-3, 3-4, 4-6, 6-5, 3-2; non-tree 1-2 and 4-5 drawn dashed '2 4' after the walk; 3-4 drawn thick domain colour and named in the note 'Bridge: 3–4' (with roads reopened). Badges '#disc ↑#low'. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G): r7: notation undecoded; legend added, ↑ replaced by ↩, 'highest' by 'earliest'. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED (stage condition). Badge values, dotted roads (non-tree 1-2 and 4-5) and the bridge marking are right (own DFS). But the legend "Depth-first from 1. #visit order; ↩ earliest # it loops back to. Dotted: road back." is the note text only when closed === null. On the natural path (tap the seven road chips, then press "Walk depth-first" without "Reopen all"), the note reads "4–6 closed: every town is still reachable." and the badges and ↩ marks appear with no legend; all three milestones are reached, so the reveal can open with the legend never shown. Also, while a road is closed it is drawn red dashed "5 5", so a closed 1-2 or 4-5 loses its "road back" dotting. Fix (builder): show the legend whenever walked (e.g. in the Walk row or as its own line), or have Walk reopen all roads; or narrow the claim to "with roads reopened".

recall.question: A network road lies on a loop of three towns. If that road is closed, what happens?
options: Nothing is cut off: traffic goes the other way round the loop
The two towns it joined are cut off from each other
It depends on how busy its towns are
recall.why: A road on a loop always has a detour, the rest of the loop. Only a bridge, a road on no loop, splits the network when closed.
